entries.value: Château Gilette ‘Crème de Tête’ Sauternes 1989 is mainly Sémillon with some Sauvignon Blanc, shrivelled by noble rot, from a tiny estate at Preignac. Its top selection, it rests close to twenty years in small concrete vats, never in oak, before bottling. Thirty-seven years on it is amber gold: crème brûlée, caramel, dried apricot, orange peel and saffron, with a surprising freshness. It is the celebration bottle for the World Famous Bananas Foster, poured after the flambé, never near the flame. We pour it at 50 to 54°F in a small white wine glass, from an ice bucket. Never ranked in 1855, Gilette is known instead for patience.

entries.value: Château d’Yquem Sauternes 2007 is Sémillon with Sauvignon Blanc from a hilltop estate in Sauternes. Pickers pass through the rows again and again for berries shrivelled by noble rot, the wine is aged in new oak, and in poor years none is made. At nineteen years: apricot, honey, candied orange, pineapple, vanilla and saffron, rich, with fresh acidity and an endless finish. It is the celebration bottle for the New Orleans Bread Pudding, a match for the custard. The sommelier presents it; small pours at 50 to 54°F in a small white wine glass, from an ice bucket. Thomas Jefferson ordered it for himself and George Washington.

entries.value: Barbadillo ‘Pale Cream’ Sherry NV is Palomino from Sanlúcar de Barrameda, at the mouth of the Guadalquivir, from a house known for Manzanilla. It starts as a light, fino-style sherry, then is gently sweetened. Pale gold and silky, it tastes of apricot, honey, almond and vanilla, with a salty, nutty edge and a soft, long finish. It suits salty plates, nuts and cheese, or alone before the meal, and is too light for the sweeter desserts. We pour it chilled, 45 to 50°F, in a small white wine glass; an opened bottle keeps a few days cold. The pale cream style dates from the 1970s.

entries.value: Feist Late Bottled Vintage Port 2006 is Port from the Douro in Portugal, red grapes of a single year bottled after four to six years in wood, where a vintage Port goes to bottle young. Twenty years on it is unusually mature for its kind: black cherry, plum, raisin, cocoa and spice, sweet and supple, with softened tannin. It is the value bottle for the Café Brûlot Coffee Cake, its chicory and bittersweet chocolate, The Snickers and the Chocolate Crémeux. We pour it at 60 to 64°F in a port glass, decanted shortly before pouring if it shows sediment. Two German cousins founded Feist in London in 1836.

entries.value: Sandeman Late Bottled Vintage Port 1999 is Port from the Douro, red grapes of one year kept four to six years in wood before bottling, and long in bottle since. At twenty-seven years, a mature garnet: dark cherry, plum, fig, spice and a little chocolate, generous, with softened tannin and a long finish. It is the value bottle for the Cherries Jubilee, meeting its black cherries and Luxardo sauce after the flambé. We stand it upright, decant it off any sediment and serve it at 60 to 64°F in a port glass. George Sandeman founded the house in London in 1790; its caped Don was drawn in 1928.
